bull.t: Strong recurring growth and customer expansion
bull.b: Rapid revenue growth, expanding large-customer adoption, and 120% dollar-based net retention show that Cloudflare is both winning new business and increasing spending within its installed base. This land-and-expand model can support durable growth across the next several quarters.

bull.t: Improving cash generation and high gross margins
bull.b: Positive and improving free cash flow demonstrates that Cloudflare’s subscription-led model is converting growth into usable cash despite accounting losses. Consistently high gross margins also provide economic capacity to fund product investment and support operating leverage over time.

Embedding continuously learning detection into Bot Management strengthens Cloudflare’s security offering as threats evolve. The use of traffic insights from its global network can improve responsiveness and product differentiation, supporting continued customer adoption of its platform.

bear.b: Cloudflare has not yet established durable GAAP profitability, and the wider TTM operating loss shows that revenue growth is not fully translating into bottom-line improvement. Continued losses can constrain financial quality and make execution on the path to profitability more important.

Relatively high leverage for a software company reduces financial flexibility and increases sensitivity if growth slows or funding conditions tighten. Modest cash-flow coverage of debt means more generated cash may need to support obligations rather than growth investments or other corporate priorities.

bear.t: Margin and cost pressure from infrastructure and restructuring
bear.b: The year-over-year gross-margin decline indicates that network-cost allocation is pressuring the economics of incremental traffic. Large restructuring charges add further earnings volatility, making sustained margin improvement and disciplined infrastructure spending key requirements for stronger profitability.
